what: 10x Genomics makes instruments and kits that analyse individual cells: which genes each cell is expressing, and where cells sit within a tissue, which is how modern biology maps disease.
customers: Academic laboratories, pharmaceutical researchers and biotech companies studying cells and tissue.
money: reagent kits used on its instruments
Chromium single cell and Xenium spatial systems
moat: Instruments placed in laboratories that then buy its consumables for years, with published papers citing its methods, which makes researchers reluctant to switch platforms.
risks: A $67M net loss and revenue roughly flat at $620M for three years
Academic funding cuts hit its main customer group directly
12 times sales for a business that is not growing
opportunities: $94M of free cash flow and $523M of cash against $84M of debt
Analysts see about 19% upside, with 14 covering the stock
Spatial biology, where Xenium competes, is the fastest-growing area in life science instruments
watch: Consumable revenue growth, which shows instrument utilisation rather than one-off sales.
